subject: NGD-247 NebulaData private offer — exec clearance for cross-cloud rev-share & discount
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@nebuladata.com>
Date: 2028-08-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: NGD-247 NebulaData private offer — request exec clearance for cross-cloud rev-share and discount

Hi Karthik / Laura —

Quick context: NebulaData is asking for an accelerated private offer across AWS + GCP to support their multi-cloud launch. They are a mid-sized analytics ISV; projected ARR year 1 = $1.2M. They want two private offers (AWS + GCP) with harmonized effective pricing and a one-time commercial concession for the first 12 months. Key asks from the customer:

- 35% off list on compute SKUs for 12 months (across both clouds)
- Rev-share carveout: request standard marketplace split be adjusted so NebulaData receives a 40% take of topline when sold via partner channel; they propose Redwood take 60% (they're asking for a partner engineering rebate on top).
- Billing terms: GCP wants Net-30, AWS prefers Net-45 (customer asks for Net-60; we should push back)
- Upfront credit: $75k against first invoice to offset onboarding support

Attached: NGD247_proposal_summary.pdf and a draft SOW (NGD247_sow.xlsx).

Ask: I need exec clearance for the nonstandard items (35% discount and the rev-share wording that splits by region/cloud). Deal desk flagged margin pressure if we accept 35% as-is. If we can get sign-off to cap discount at 30% and approve the rev-share harmonization with specific % by cloud, we can move to marketplace ops + legal to build the private offers.

Proposed internal compromise (for signoff):
- Discount: approve up to 30% for 12 months (no extension without exec re-approval)
- Rev-share (Redwood : NebulaData): AWS 65:35, GCP 70:30.
- Upfront credit: $50k (not $75k) subject to finance approval and clawback if churn > 40% in first 6 months
- Billing: AWS Net-45, GCP Net-30

Please advise next steps — if this looks okay I’ll route to Marissa + Markus for final exec OK.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: NGD247_proposal_summary.pdf (pdf), NGD247_sow.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-22T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NGD-247 NebulaData private offer — request exec clearance for cross-cloud rev-share & discount

Eve —

Thanks for the clear summary. I ran a quick margin model and 35% consistently pushes us below our target unit economics for both AWS and GCP once marketplace fees and estimated egress are accounted for. The split Nebula is asking (40% to them) would be okay only if we retain a higher list or get a fixed engineering rebate from Nebula (we do not have that commitment).

Deal desk recommendation:
- Discount cap: 25% unconditional; escalate for 30% with exec approval and the upfront credit reduced to $50k.
- Rev-share: we can accept a temporary variance but need it carved per-cloud in the private offers. Suggested rev-share (Redwood:Nebula): AWS 65:35, GCP 68:32.
- Require an audit clause and churn-based clawback for the upfront credit (standard wording).

I’ve attached a short analysis (deal_desk_analysis.csv) with projected margin / payback windows. If you can loop in Marissa + Markus and ask for a decision on 30% vs 25%, we’ll prep the marketplace ops runbook.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
Attachments: deal_desk_analysis.csv (csv)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia@nebuladata.com>
Date: 2028-08-22T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: NGD-247 NebulaData — Exec approval needed (AWS + GCP private offers)

Marissa —

Forwarding the thread. Short bullets for exec consideration:
- NebulaData wants cross-cloud private offers (AWS + GCP) with a 35% introductory discount + $75k onboarding credit.
- Deal desk recommends lowering discount to 25% (or 30% with exec OK) and proposes cloud-specific rev-share splits to preserve unit economics.
- Customer timeline: they want the offers live before their Sept 20 product launch.

Specific decision points for you and Markus:
1) Approve 30% discount for 12 months (conditional approval) OR instruct we cap at 25%
2) Approve per-cloud rev-share variances (confirm percentages).
3) Approve upfront credit of $50k vs customer request of $75k.

If we get a thumbs up on 30% + the rev-share split, marketplace ops will need an explicit clause: offers auto-revert to standard terms after 12 months and include an audit/clawback for the upfront credit. Also we need Legal to approve the wording for rev-share tracking by listing ID.

Link to deal in HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deals/NGD-247
Docsend (proposal): https://docsend.com/view/ngd247-proposal

Evelyn

Evelyn / team —

I’ll approve a conditional concession to enable the launch, with the following mandatory controls in place before we finalize:

1) Discount: Approve up to 30% off list for 12 months only. No extensions without renewed exec approval.
2) Rev-share by cloud (fixed in contract):
   - AWS private offer: Redwood:NebulaData = 65:35
   - GCP private offer: Redwood:NebulaData = 68:32
3) Upfront credit: Approve $50,000 only. Clawback clause required if customer churn > 40% in the first 6 months.
4) Billing terms: Approve AWS Net-45, GCP Net-30 as a compromise.
5) Marketplace ops must create two separate private offers and include an explicit auto-revert clause (after 12 months returns to standard marketplace splits).
6) Legal must insert an audit right and reporting cadence (monthly rev-share reports by listing ID).
7) Finance (Markus) to sign off on accounting treatment for the upfront credit and provide invoice code for tracking.

Actions assigned:
- Laura: create the AWS + GCP private offer tickets, include SKU price floors and the auto-revert clause.
- Karthik: finalize deal desk margin note and coordinate with Legal on clawback language.
- Aditya: validate EDP/engineering rebate ask (if Nebula offers an engineering co-invest, reduce our concession).
- Evelyn: communicate conditional approval to the customer and confirm DocuSign flow.

Once Markus confirms finance treatment, we can mark this as exec-cleared. I’ve attached a short approval note.

Marissa
Marissa Cole

Marissa / team —

I’m good to sign off on the conditional approval Marissa outlined with two finance caveats:

1) Upfront credit accounting: The $50k onboarding credit will be capitalized and amortized over the first 12 months. Finance will require a clawback schedule in the contract to reverse any amortization pro rata if the customer churns > 40% in the first 6 months.
2) Rev-share tracking: We will create a dedicated invoice code (INV-NGD247) and require Marketplace ops to push consolidated monthly rev-share reports to finance@redwood.com by the 10th of each month. If rev-share reporting is delayed more than 2 cycles, we will reserve the right to pause credits.

Financial approvals: AWS Net-45 (approved), GCP Net-30 (approved). Please ensure marketplace ops include the listing IDs and any reseller flow so we can reconcile.

Evelyn — please send the conditional approval to NebulaData with the exact wording below and attach the SOW + approval note. Once the DocuSign is executed we can book the revenue plan.

Approved (subject to legal wording and DocuSign):
- Discount: 30% off list for 12 months
- Rev-share per-cloud: AWS 65:35 / GCP 68:32
- Upfront credit: $50,000 with clawback
- Billing: AWS Net-45, GCP Net-30

-Markus
